validation_scope: Source-reviewed examples for one MISP instance. Rendering and book-format checks exercise the documentation, not a new live publication, proposal or delegation integration test.
assumptions: Alice and Bob share Org A. Bob can review and publish that organization's event. Their review handoff is manual.
The proposal author in Org B can see the event and submit a proposal. Org A has the permissions to accept/discard and publish. Cross-instance proposal transport is outside the sequence.
The delegation source and recipient are local organizations. The source uses an eligible organization-only draft. Recipient review/acceptance and later publication remain separate.
Publication state, analysis level, distribution, IDS eligibility, notification preferences and successful delivery are separate decisions.
checked_behavior: Normal event-form editing clears published. Accepted attribute proposals apply the change and call unpublishEvent. The diagrams avoid the historical assertion that every kind of attached-data change is an event edit.
Publication permission and event access are checked. The optional block_publishing_for_same_creator setting defaults false and compares the publisher with the recorded event creator.
publishRouter can enqueue a job. The published flag alone does not establish delivery to a remote instance or detector.
Delegation transfer changes org_id and orgc_id and saves the event with its UUID. Acceptance does not itself execute publication or apply the requested distribution.
